name: basecraft-sanderson-native
validation: macOS engine unit tests: 6 passed, 1 diagnostic benchmark ignored (release, M1, macOS 15.5). Same source and Cargo.lock hashes as the reference-validated Linux engine. Outputs compared with the validated Linux binary on deterministic fixtures (generate_fixture.py: 8-tip clock, 64-tip nonclock, 64-tip nonclock with a 4-point CV grid, 512-tip nonclock; log penalty): identical accepted starts; largest relative difference over 2868 estimates 5.6e-5 (8-tip case identical). 64-tip additive-penalty fixture: both reach the same optimum (objectives agree to 1e-12), but the strict gradient gate accepts start 3 on macOS (4.95e-5 vs tolerance 5.08e-5) and rejects it on Linux (5.16e-5), so Linux returns no converged start. Normal-dependency closure for aarch64-apple-darwin (47 crates) equals Linux's and is covered by the Linux notice inventory.
pending: Independent scientific review of this cross-platform evidence, including the borderline convergence gate.
